hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM trained with lambdarank over user-groups capped at 6 consecutive rows (matching the ~5.6-row valid lists), on base5 plus within-user duration features, will beat the 0.6016 baseline substantially.
rationale: The baseline optimises pointwise logloss while the metric is a within-user ordering metric [POINTWISE_BASELINE]; lambdarank's gradient is driven by pairwise swaps inside a list, which is exactly the quantity GAUC and nDCG@5 measure. Capping groups at 6 makes the training list length and the position discount match the evaluation list length instead of the 43.5-row training lists [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH], so the discount the model optimises is the one it is scored under [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]. Adding dur_feats gives the tree an explicitly within-user-varying signal: long_view is a watch-length threshold, so a video's duration percentile inside the user's own impression list is close to a direct prior on the label, and unlike the coarse dur_bucket already in base5 it is comparable across users.
expected_gain_derivation: Three effects stack. (a) Loss change: the organizers list loss function first among unexplored directions [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] and pairwise-vs-pointwise swaps on short lists typically move ranking metrics by 0.01-0.03. (b) Grouping: training on 43.5-row lists when scoring 5.6-row lists mis-specifies the discount [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]; correcting it is worth maybe 0.005-0.01. (c) dur_feats: duration is the mechanistic driver of long_view and the percentile version varies within user [WITHIN_USER_RANKING], unlike user_agg which cannot reorder anything [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]; worth ~0.01-0.02. Total ~0.04, far above the 0.0008 seed noise floor [SEED_NOISE], and still only a quarter of the way to the 0.8484 ceiling [CEILING].

block_justifications.base5: It is the exact field set the 0.6016 baseline uses, so holding it fixed makes this run a clean read on the model/objective/grouping switch; video_id and author_id also vary within a user's list and therefore can reorder it [WITHIN_USER_RANKING].
block_justifications.dur_feats: long_view is a watch-length threshold, so duration percentile computed inside the user's own list is a within-user-varying prior on the label and is the concrete instance of the duration-bias direction the organizers left unexplored [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].

hypothesis: Adding out-of-fold train-window item aggregates (video/author long-view rate, click rate, impression count) to the LightGBM lambdarank/chunk-6 setup will lift validation primary well above the 0.6018 the same setup reached without them.
rationale: In a ~6-row valid list the only things that vary within the user are which videos/authors were shown and how long they are. Raw video_id as a categorical with max_cat_threshold=64 cannot express per-item quality for tens of thousands of sparsely observed levels; an OOF long-view rate hands the tree that same quantity as a dense monotone numeric that generalises to the 99.9% of valid videos seen in train [HIGH_COVERAGE]. This is the single largest piece of within-user-varying signal not currently reachable by the model.
expected_gain_derivation: Iteration 1 moved only +0.0004 over baseline, so the objective/grouping switch alone bought almost nothing, which means the frame is information-starved rather than loss-misspecified. The remaining unexploited within-user signal is item identity quality [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]; base5 already contains video_id so part of it is present, but only as a high-cardinality split that LightGBM under-uses. With 99.9% valid-video coverage in train [HIGH_COVERAGE] a dense OOF item rate should recover most of that. Baseline-to-ceiling headroom is 0.8484-0.6016 = 0.247 [CEILING]; I estimate this feature captures ~6% of it, i.e. ~0.015, far above the 0.0008 noise floor [SEED_NOISE].

block_justifications.base5: Held fixed from iteration 1 so that this run is a single-block read on item_agg [ONE_CHANGE_PER_SPEC]; video_id/author_id/tab vary within a user's list and can therefore reorder it [WITHIN_USER_RANKING].
block_justifications.dur_feats: Also carried over unchanged from iteration 1 to preserve attribution; duration is the mechanistic driver of a watch-length threshold label and its within-user percentile varies across the list [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].
block_justifications.item_agg: The one changed block: an OOF long-view/click rate per video and author is a dense within-user-varying estimate of item quality that the sparse video_id categorical cannot express, and it transfers because 99.9% of valid videos appear in train [HIGH_COVERAGE].

hypothesis: Switching to a listwise objective (rank_xendcg) and adding the personalised cross_agg block (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, and duration relative to the user's own historically long-viewed duration) will finally move validation primary meaningfully above 0.6021.
rationale: Everything tried so far encodes item-side or list-side properties that are shared by all users; iteration 1 (loss+grouping) and iteration 2 (item quality) each moved <0.0005, which says the frame is starved of the one thing that actually differentiates rows inside a single user's ~6-item list: how well THIS item matches THIS user. cross_agg is the only available block that is both user-personalised and within-user varying, and its duration-relative-to-user-habit component is the direct mechanistic model of a watch-length threshold label (a 60s video is a long_view for a user who habitually watches long, not for a skimmer). Pairing it with rank_xendcg changes the loss from pairwise-with-a-position-discount to a listwise softmax over the whole group, which is the better match to a metric that is half GAUC (no discount at all) and half nDCG@5 over ~6 items (effectively order-the-whole-list).
expected_gain_derivation: Headroom is 0.8484-0.6021 = 0.246 [CEILING]. item_agg captured ~0.0003 of it, which tells me impersonal item quality is nearly exhausted and the residual is personalisation. Within-user preference matching is the largest untouched axis that is not user-constant [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] and is exactly the duration-bias / behaviour direction the organizers flagged [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED]; I put it at ~2.5% of remaining headroom = 0.006. The loss switch adds little on its own (iteration 1 showed the objective axis is worth <0.001 here) but rank_xendcg with no position discount is better matched to the GAUC half of the metric [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS], so I attribute ~0.001 of the 0.006 to it. 0.006 is well clear of the 0.0008 seed-noise floor [SEED_NOISE] and clears the 0.0014 I need over current best to keep the window open [CONVERGENCE_MECHANICS].

block_justifications.base5: video_id, author_id, tab and dur_bucket vary within a user's list and so are the only base fields that can reorder it [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]; keeping them means the new block is measured as an addition to the known 0.6021 frame rather than against an amputated one.
block_justifications.dur_feats: long_view is a watch-length threshold, so log-duration and the within-user duration percentile are the mechanical prior on the label and were already part of the 0.6021 frame.
block_justifications.item_agg: Carried from iteration 2 where it was measured as mildly positive; 99.9% of valid videos appear in train so the OOF item long-view rate transfers [HIGH_COVERAGE].
block_justifications.cross_agg: The substantive change: user x author and user x tag affinity plus duration-relative-to-the-user's-own-long-viewed-duration are personalised and vary across the user's rows, which is the only remaining signal class that can reorder a list once impersonal item quality is exhausted [WITHIN_USER_RANKING].
